abstract.para: This procedure explains how to configure &qdevice; after the cluster is already installed and running, not during the initial cluster setup.

listitem.para: An existing &ha; cluster is already running.
The latest corosync-qdevice package is installed on all nodes.
The latest corosync-qnetd package is installed on the &qnet; server.
To connect to the &qnet; server as a sudo user: The user must have passwordless sudo permission.
To connect to the &qnet; server as the &rootuser; user: Passwordless SSH authentication must be configured between the nodes and the &qnet; server.

topic.para: Perform this procedure on only one cluster node:

step.para: Log in either as the &rootuser; user or as a user with sudo privileges.
Check whether any resources are running:
Run the &qdevice; stage of the cluster setup script, using the option --qnetd-hostname to specify the IP address or host name of the &qnet; server:

listitem.para: If you include a non-&rootuser; user name, a later step will prompt you for the user's password and the script will configure passwordless SSH authentication from the nodes to the &qnet; server.
If you omit a user name, the script defaults to the &rootuser; user, so passwordless SSH authentication must already be configured for the nodes to access the &qnet; server.

variablelist.title: Additional options
variablelist.para: The setup script automatically uses the default values for the &qdevice; configuration. If you need to change any of these settings, you can use the following options:

listitem.para: The default is 5403. You can use the --qnetd-port option to specify a different port.
The default is ffsplit. You can use the --qdevice-algo option to specify a different algorithm.

ffsplit (fifty-fifty split): If the cluster splits into two even partitions, one of the partitions gets the vote based on the results of heuristics checks and other factors. This algorithm is helpful for clusters with an even number of nodes.

lms (last man standing): If only one remaining node can still communicate with the &qnet; server, that node gets the vote. This algorithm is helpful for clusters where only one active node needs to remain quorate.
The default is lowest. You can use the --qdevice-tie-breaker option to specify a different method.
lowest: The node with the lowest node ID gets the vote.
highest: The node with the highest node ID gets the vote.
Alternatively, you can set a specific node ID. The designated node always gets the vote.
The default is on. You can use the --qdevice-tls option to specify a different setting.
off: TLS isn't required and shouldn't be tried.
on: Attempt to connect with TLS, but connect without TLS if it isn't available.
required: TLS is mandatory, so &qdevice; exits with an error if TLS isn't available.

You can use the --qdevice-heuristics option to specify heuristics commands to assist in quorum calculation. You can enter one command, multiple commands separated by semicolons, or the path to a script file. The commands can be written in any programming language.
If you use heuristics commands, you must also use the --qdevice-heuristics-mode option to specify the mode of operation. The default is sync.
sync: &qdevice; runs heuristics when the cluster services start (or restart), when the cluster membership changes, and when nodes connect to the &qnet; server.
on: &qdevice; runs heuristics in the same scenarios as sync and also at regular intervals.

step.para: If required, the script prompts you for the password of the &qnet; server, then configures passwordless SSH authentication between the cluster nodes and the &qnet; server.
The script configures &qdevice; on the nodes, completes the &qnet; server's configuration, and restarts the cluster services.
